title.en: A vow made in a hospital bed

text.en: Imagine lying in a hospital bed after losing a leg and promising yourself that you will climb the highest mountain in the world. Most people would call that impossible. This chapter is the true story of Arunima Sinha, who did exactly that.

You identify adventure activities from icons, discuss why people undertake them, how they prepare, and which seems the most exciting, and complete a word web on adventure.
The chapter says this is a story of will, courage, determination and dedication. Arunima Sinha is a beacon of hope and resilience, which means a source of inspiration and the ability to recover quickly from a difficulty. In 2011, at the age of 24, she was a national-level volleyball player when a life-altering event changed everything. As she lay in hospital with one leg amputated, she vowed to walk again with a prosthetic leg, which is an artificial leg, and to climb Mount Everest. In 2013 she did, becoming the first Indian female amputee to climb Everest. In 2015 she received the Padma Shri, the fourth highest civilian award in India. She also received the Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Award and the National Award for Best Female Mountaineer.
Arunima comes from Ambedkar Nagar, a small district in Uttar Pradesh. Her father was an army engineer and her mother a health supervisor, and sports were a big part of the family's life. After a post-graduation and a law degree, she decided to seek a job in the paramilitary forces, which would let her continue her passion for sports and have a regular income. On the night of 11 April 2011, she met with a train accident. The hours that followed were harrowing, which means extremely disturbing and painful. She did not imagine she would survive, but she miraculously did, showing an extraordinary will to live.
She received a prosthetic leg and underwent physiotherapy. During this time, inspired by an article about Mount Everest, she resolved to climb the highest peak in the world. She completed a basic mountaineering course at the Nehru Institute of Mountaineering in Uttarkashi and then eighteen months of rigorous training. She approached Bachendri Pal, the first Indian woman to reach the summit of Everest, for guidance. Bachendri Pal gave her confidence. She said that Arunima had decided to climb Everest in such a situation with a prosthetic leg, so she had conquered the Everest within herself, and the world would realise it later.
On 21 May 2013, after 52 exhausting days, Arunima reached the summit of Mount Everest. She felt a surge of emotions, pride, relief and an overwhelming sense of achievement. She displayed the Indian flag at the summit and left a photograph of her idol, Swami Vivekananda, whose teachings had inspired her. She did not stop there. By July 2016 she had climbed the highest peaks of Europe, Africa, Australia, South America, North America and Asia. In January 2019 she climbed Mount Vinson in Antarctica, the seventh, and became the world's first female amputee to do so. She had completed the Seven Summits.
Her story is not only about physical endurance but also about mental fortitude, which is courage over a long time, and a positive mindset. Her message is to never give up, work hard and always remember your goal. Her autobiography, Born Again on the Mountain: A Story of Losing Everything and Finding It Back, records her journey. The title is fitting, because she lost her leg and her old life, then found new purpose on the mountain. She was given an honorary doctorate by the University of Strathclyde in Glasgow. Her thought that failure is not falling short but not having goals worthy enough inspires readers to aim high. She has won hearts around the world and inspires others to reach their own summits.
She is a beacon of hope because, despite losing a leg, she trained for years, climbed Everest and then six more summits. Her decision to climb despite her loss, Bachendri Pal's guidance, her mental strength and her book all show that her achievement goes beyond physical endurance. The phrase 52 exhausting days shows how tiring the climb was. After her success she would most likely say, I finally realised my dream. Word meanings: exhausting days are periods filled with tiring and demanding activity, heartfelt attempts are genuine, sincere efforts, a life-altering event significantly changes a person's life, mental fortitude is strength of mind, and a beacon of hope is a source of inspiration. Word forms: determination is a noun, determine is a verb, and determined is an adjective. Practise forming nouns, verbs and adjectives of words such as achieve and inspire.

why.en: She decided to climb despite her prosthetic leg.

prompt.en: Describe how Arunima Sinha prepared for and achieved her goal, and what she teaches us.

requiredIdeas.en: She lost a leg in a train accident in 2011.
She trained at the Nehru Institute of Mountaineering and with Bachendri Pal.
She reached the summit of Everest on 21 May 2013 and later completed the Seven Summits.
She teaches us to never give up and to have worthy goals.

commonMisconceptions.en: She climbed Everest before the accident.
She was the first Indian woman on Everest.

points.en: Arunima Sinha lost a leg in a train accident in 2011 and vowed to climb Everest.
She trained hard, and reached the summit on 21 May 2013.
She completed the Seven Summits and wrote an autobiography.
Her message is to never give up and to set goals worthy of your effort.
Words such as beacon, harrowing, fortitude and adversity enrich our vocabulary.
